topics.title: Tables: table, tr, th, td, thead, tbody, tfoot
topics.summary: Tables show two-dimensional data using rows and cells, grouped into head, body and foot.
topics.description:
The `<table>` element presents **tabular data** - information with rows and columns, like a price list, timetable or score board. It must **not** be used for page layout (use CSS Grid/Flexbox for that).

### The building blocks
| Element | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `<table>` | The whole table |
| `<tr>` | A table **r**ow |
| `<th>` | A **h**eader cell (bold, centred by default) |
| `<td>` | A **d**ata cell |
| `<thead>` | Group of header rows |
| `<tbody>` | Group of body rows (main data) |
| `<tfoot>` | Group of footer rows (totals) |

### How rows and cells combine
A table is built **row by row**: each `<tr>` holds `<th>` or `<td>` cells. There is no "column" element for data - the columns come from the cells lined up in each row.

### Why thead/tbody/tfoot?
They give structure: browsers can repeat the header on each printed page, assistive technology understands the roles, and you can style groups easily (`tbody tr:nth-child(even)` for zebra stripes).

### Styling
Default tables have no borders. Add them with CSS. `border-collapse: collapse` merges double borders into one.

### Deprecated attributes
`border`, `cellpadding`, `cellspacing`, `bgcolor`, `align`, `width` on table elements are obsolete. Do all presentation with CSS.
keyPoints: Use tables only for tabular data, never for layout.
tr = row; th = header cell; td = data cell.
thead / tbody / tfoot give the table structure.
Style with CSS (border-collapse, padding); old attributes are deprecated.
pitfalls: Using td with bold text instead of a real th.
Putting content directly in tr without a cell.

interview.q: Purpose of thead, tbody and tfoot?
interview.a: They group header rows, main data rows and footer rows, giving structure for styling, accessibility and printing.
th is a header cell (bold, centred, announced as a header by screen readers); td is an ordinary data cell.

interview.q: Should tables be used for page layout?
interview.a: No. Tables are for tabular data; use CSS Flexbox or Grid for layout.

topics.title: colspan & rowspan (Merging Cells)
topics.summary: Make a cell span several columns or rows to build timetables and grouped headings.
topics.description:
Sometimes one cell must be wider or taller than the grid - a title across all columns, or a "Lunch" break that spans the whole day. Two attributes handle this.

- `colspan="n"` - the cell stretches over **n columns** (to the right).
- `rowspan="n"` - the cell stretches over **n rows** (downwards).

### Counting rule
Every row must "add up" to the same number of columns. A cell with `colspan="3"` counts as three cells; a cell with `rowspan="2"` also occupies a slot in the next row, so that row needs **one fewer** cell.

### Example plan - a timetable
```
| timetable (colspan 7)              |
| hours (rowspan 4) | Mon Tue Wed ... |
|                   | math math ...   |
|                   | Lunch (colspan 6) |
```

### Tips
- Draw the grid on paper first and count cells.
- Do not leave a row with too many or too few cells - the table will look broken.
- Heavy use of spans makes tables hard for screen readers; add `scope` / `headers` (see the accessibility topic) or simplify the table.
- For header cells that group columns use `<th colspan="2" scope="colgroup">`.

### colspan vs CSS
colspan and rowspan describe **data structure**, so they belong in HTML; the visual look stays in CSS.
keyPoints: colspan merges cells horizontally, rowspan vertically.
Each row must add up to the same total columns.
A rowspan cell removes a cell from the following rows.
Use th with scope for spanning headers.
pitfalls: Forgetting to remove cells in rows covered by a rowspan.
Putting colspan larger than the number of columns.
Overusing spans making the table inaccessible.

interview.q: What do colspan and rowspan do?
interview.a: colspan makes a cell span multiple columns; rowspan makes a cell span multiple rows.

interview.q: Why is a table with rowspan sometimes broken?
interview.a: Rows covered by a rowspan must have one fewer cell; wrong counts shift cells out of place.

topics.title: Accessible Tables: caption, scope, colgroup & Responsiveness
topics.summary: Add caption, scope, headers and colgroup so tables make sense to everyone, and handle small screens.
topics.description:

interview.q: What is the scope attribute for?
interview.a: It declares whether a th is a header for a column, row or group, so assistive tech can announce proper headers for each cell.

interview.q: How do you make a table responsive for small screens?
interview.a: Wrap it in a container with overflow-x:auto, or restyle rows as stacked blocks with CSS.
As the first child of the table element.
